10042351:
Addison Verrill Pittsfield LD 1121
To Whom It May Concern,
My name is Addison Verrill, and I live in the town of Pittsfield. I am currently a first-year student at Dartmouth College in Hanover, New Hampshire. I am testifying in support of LD-1121.
My grandfather never changed my mother's diaper. His father had never changed his. In fact, my mother was toilet trained within two days when my grandmother went to work after my grandfather's union went on strike. He refused to change her diapers, despite the fact that he was, for that period, a stay-at-home dad. That was in the late `70's. Years have passed, and times have thankfully changed. This is no longer the reality. My father stayed home with my sister in her infancy while my mother worked. He learned to change diapers. He changed mine as well. The new reality is that both partners in a new family contribute to basic childcare, and that includes changing diapers.
However, public infrastructure does not reflect this reality. Public places often only have changing stations in the women's restroom or in a family restroom (if they have one), and not all places have such facilities. If a father is out with a baby, or maybe multiple babies, where can they change diapers?
Even if a mother or grandmother is with them, this lack of changing stations in all bathrooms promotes the inequitable distribution of childcare between parents, supporting the idea that the mother is the caregiver and the father need not worry themselves about such things. However supportive of equality the men in our society may be, they are forced to hand the baby off to their partner to change diapers because they do not have the facilities to do it themselves. While it may seem like a very small thing, this is a very important step in order to work toward a fair society in our state. Although this bill would not mandate changing stations in all public places, putting them in state buildings would set a strong tone to move toward a more balanced division in childcare and create a precedent for businesses around the state to follow the example of the legislature.
I appreciate your consideration of LD-1121, and I hope that you will support this bill as it advances the goals of equity. Thank you.
10041100:
Anne M. Gallaudet Scarborough, Maine
March 31, 2025
Re: LD 1121 An Act to Ensure Equitable Access for All Caregivers to Diaper Changing Stations in State Buildings Open to the Public
Senator Baldacci, Representative Salisbury and Honorable Members of the Joint State and Local Government Committee
I appreciate this opportunity to address you on this important matter. My name is Anne Gallaudet. I am a resident of Scarborough, Maine. I am writing in support of LD 1121.
Federal law does not require diaper changing stations in men's bathrooms. The Bathroom Accessible in Every Situation Act (BABIES) Act does require diaper changing stations in men's bathrooms in federal buildings. https://prestigedistribution.com/pages/baby-changing-stationlaws?srsltid=AfmBOoqrWWF2SingAMU5zO_CAY3JowZjajqM2tkVXHqOfirzoeYuG5d; https://www.koalabear.com/product-resources/changing-stationresources-landing-page/compliance-homepage/legislation-map/
LD 1121 addresses a vital issue facing caregivers and parents when young children visiting public state buildings need their diapers changed. We no longer can turn a blind eye to the fact that many of the parents or caretakers are men. Too often they lack access to an appropriate site. Having access to diaper changing stations if the need arises while conducting business at a state building is reasonable, appropriate and shows consideration for the public.
Specifically, access to a convenient diaper changing station outside of family diaper changing rooms or female restrooms with such stations provides needed parity for all men who care for children, as parents or caregivers. It also ensures that no child is forced to wear dirty diapers because of lack of access to an appropriate diaper changing station or be changed in a dirty environment, such as in a car or on the ground. Moreover, this bill provides consideration for our citizens trying to conduct state business while meeting their childcare responsibilities. It ensures they do not have to leave the building merely to change a diaper or do so in an unsanitary and/or unnecessary inconvenient manner. Passing this bill will also enhance the image of our state as supporting all parents and childcare providers.

Even 40 years ago when I was raising my young children, my husband equally shared childcare responsibilities while I worked full time. Access to appropriate diaper changing stations for him was extremely difficult and many times our children were changed in the public - in our car, on the ground, on a stroller with the back leaning back, on the floor in public spaces, etc. Things should be quite different today, but it is shocking how so little has changed in 40 years. Diaper changing stations are essential and all caregivers must have access to such in state buildings.
Thank you for considering my appeal. I urge you to vote "Ought to Pass" on LD 1121.
Anne Gallaudet, Scarborough, ME
10041102:
March 31st, 2025
Senator Baldacci , Representative Salisbury, and Honorable Members of the State and Local Government Committee,
I join you today on behalf of the Maine Women's Lobby. For over forty years, the Maine Women's Lobby has worked to build gender justice in Maine through legislative advocacy and systems change.
We are here today in support of LD 1121, "An Act to Ensure Equitable Access for All Caregivers to Diaper Changing Stations in State Buildings Open to the Public" and we thank Representative Collamore for sponsoring this important bill. We were deeply grateful that this committee voted "Ought to Pass" on a similar bill last session and are hopeful for your remaining commitment on this proposal.
When Maine Women's Lobby hosts an advocacy day at the State House, we send out a document we call the "Maine State House Survival Guide" which includes a wide range of information on accessibility, such as where elevators are located, where someone can find a gender neutral bathroom and where someone can chestfeed. We share this info because we know that government buildings were not designed with inclusivity and accessibility in mind, and that many need this type of information to know how to prepare for their time at the State House.
Lack of accessible infrastructure for parents and caregivers can be a barrier for parents, caregivers and families. Recognizing the importance of accessibility for parents, in 2014, Congress passed the Bathroom Accessible In Every Situation Act (BABIES Act)1, which requires baby changing stations in federal buildings. Beyond this, diaper changing station regulations vary from state to state and even county to county.
While general availability of changing stations is important, ensuring parents and caregivers are able to access changing stations in state-owned buildings would go a long way to ensuring that parents and caregivers voices, perspectives and participation is included and valued. There is a general lack of such perspectives in the State Legislature, for example, with only 6.75% of legislators in Maine are women with children under eighteen.2
Further, ensuring availability of changing stations in bathrooms that are located in areas accessible by all genders is critical to promoting gender equity so that all parents have equal opportunity to care for their children. It also acknowledges the variety of family and caregiving structures, and moves away from antiquated gender roles predicated on stereotypical "women's roles" and family structures. This inclusivity is key to ensuring the long term efficacy of this proposal and ensuring ALL families, parents and caregivers have the same opportunities.
We hope you will vote Ought to Pass on LD 1121. Thank you for your consideration. Lily Bohen James, Maine Women's Lobby

March 31, 2025

Senator Baldacci, Representative Salisbury and members of the Joint Standing Committee on
State and Local Government, my name is Mattie Daughtry. I sen/e as President of the Maine
Senate and proudly represent Senate District 23 in the Legislature, which includes Brunswick,
Freeport, Harpswell, Pownal, Chebeague Island, and part of Yarmouth. I am here to testify in support of LD 1121, "An Act to Ensure Equitable Access for All Caregivers to Diaper Changing
Stations in State Buildings Open to the Public."
This bill simply requires that public buildings in Maine have diaper changing stations in men's and women's bathrooms. This bill will not require costly renovations for older buildings but only applies to new construction.

Equal access to changing stations is already required for federal buildings. Additionally, nine states have already enacted similar legislation and two more have bills before their Legislatures
this year. It surprises me that Maine, and every state, does not already have this type of law on the
books.
Often, because changing stations are in women's restrooms but not men's, the burden of changing diapers falls on women. When fathers come to state buildings with a young baby, they should have the same tools to care for their little one as a mother. By making this slight change in Maine, we set a good example that shows Maine's commitment to all caretakers. This bill requires that stations are included in bathrooms that are accessible by men and women, in order to make sure
that parents can provide care for their children.

When I became Senate President, I wanted to find ways to make the Maine Legislature more accessible and transparent for Mainers from all walks of life. If you're a father who is passionate about a bill coming here to testify with your child, we can break down this one barrier to make the building more accessible to all. To me, this is a small actionable change that I am glad to see Rep. Collamore introduce. I am pleased to support it.

Again, I am so glad that this bill has been brought forward. Thank you for your time and consideration. I am happy to take questions.

10042253:
Riley Nelson Pittsfield, ME
April 3, 2025
RE: LD 1121 An Act to Ensure Equitable Access for All Caregivers to Diaper Changing Stations in State Buildings Open to the Public
Senator Baldacci, Representative Salisbury, and Honorable Members of the Joint State and Local Government Committee,
My Name is Riley Nelson. You may or may not know me as the then high school student, and member of Maine District 68, as Represented by Representative Amanda Collamore, who helped author the 131st's LD 93, the foundation and inspiration for this very bill you have before you.
It has been two years since this bill was first authored, and a year since it was introduced at the State House, where, as LD 93, it was passed to be enacted, and subsequently died when it was not funded.
I urge that you vote ought to pass on LD 1121. There is more than enough precedent based upon the federal B.A.B.I.E.S act, and the several other U.S. States that have similar legislation. These include but are not limited to: California HSC�118506, Illinois Public Act 101-0293, and Nevada AB 241.
This is an issue of both equality and equity. We as a state have long been a leader in the realm of equal rights, and it is deeply encoded into our legislation and state constitution. This legislation is important for equality and balanced parenthood responsibility. Beyond this, it is important to consider the gay adoptive dads of our state, who do not have any access to changing stations whatsoever. This puts them and their child at undue risk. And what about the single fathers who are just trying to do right by their child? What should they do?
This is also an issue of health and safety, namely for the infant to have a clean place to be changed, but also for the public who currently are faced with dads who are forced to change their children on store shelves or bathroom sinks.
As this bill stands it is a huge step in the correct direction by requiring changing stations be accessible to all in state buildings. It is a step towards measures other states have already taken, which require changing stations in all public restrooms. It is a step forward. A step for what's right. This should not be a divisive idea. This is a human fact of life, and a need for all.
As a man who hopes to one day be a father in our lovely state, I once again urge you to vote ought to pass on LD 1121, as the 131st did for LD 93.
Thank you.
-Riley Nelson, Pittsfield, ME
